nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Warm tropical sunshine drives algae in the shallow, sediment-rich lake and plants on the floodplain.

nodes.name: Seasonal flood pulse
nodes.desc: Monsoon rains reverse the flow of the Tonlé Sap River, and the lake swells from roughly 2,500 km2 to over 16,000 km2, drowning forest and fields.

nodes.name: Mekong sediment and nutrients
nodes.desc: Floodwater from the Mekong carries silt and nutrients into the lake; sediment-bound phosphorus helps feed its algae.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals on the floodplain and lake bed, returning nutrients to the sediment.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae in the turbid lake water; sediment-bound phosphorus and internal nutrient cycling support their growth.

nodes.name: Flooded-forest tree
nodes.desc: A tree of the seasonally flooded forest that rings the lake and shelters young fish when the water rises.

nodes.name: Wild and cultivated rice
nodes.desc: Wild rice and rice paddies cover parts of the floodplain and feed insects, rodents and wading birds.

nodes.name: Strawberry tree
nodes.desc: A fast-growing fruit tree of village edges and dry land around the lake, eaten by fruit bats.

nodes.name: Zooplankton
nodes.desc: Tiny drifting animals that graze algae and are eaten by fish larvae and small fish.

nodes.name: Mekong giant catfish
nodes.desc: One of the largest freshwater fish; after its first year it mostly feeds on algae. Found in the Tonlé Sap, but now rare.

nodes.name: Climbing perch
nodes.desc: A hardy small fish of ponds, swamps and paddies; prey for otters and many wading birds.

nodes.name: Grey pansy
nodes.desc: A butterfly whose caterpillars feed on rice and other plants of open, wet ground.

nodes.name: Ricefield rat
nodes.desc: A rodent of rice fields and wet grassland that eats rice and is prey for snakes, birds and otters.

nodes.name: Lyle's flying fox
nodes.desc: A large fruit bat of Cambodia and nearby countries that roosts in trees and feeds on fruit such as strawberry tree.

nodes.name: Asian grass frog
nodes.desc: A common frog of paddies and wet ground that eats insects and is itself prey for snakes and birds.

nodes.name: Rainbow water snake
nodes.desc: A freshwater snake of Southeast Asian wetlands that hunts fish and frogs.

nodes.name: Painted stork
nodes.desc: Wading bird that sweeps its bill through shallows for small fish and frogs; nests in colonies in trees near water.

nodes.name: Oriental darter
nodes.desc: Swims with only its neck above water and spears fish; nests in mixed waterbird colonies in trees standing in water.

nodes.name: Giant snakehead
nodes.desc: A voracious freshwater predator that eats nearly anything small enough to fit in its mouth and can gulp air in poor water.

nodes.name: Greater adjutant
nodes.desc: A very rare stork that scavenges carrion and also eats frogs, rodents and fish. Cambodia, including Tonlé Sap, is one of its last breeding areas.

nodes.name: Siamese crocodile
nodes.desc: Critically endangered freshwater crocodile that eats fish and snakes plus amphibians and small mammals.

nodes.name: Smooth-coated otter
nodes.desc: Family-group otter of wetlands and rivers that hunts mainly fish and also takes rats in paddies.
